title: The Cast

description.main: The Cast (2017) collects Dutch artist Ruth van Beek's sculptural collages built from found photographs — botanical and craft images reworked with cut paper and paint into biomorphic, almost animate forms.
description.extended:
The Cast (2017) collects Ruth van Beek's (b. 1977) sculptural collages built from an archive of found photographs, botanical and craft images clipped from vintage books and magazines, physically reworked into biomorphic, almost animate forms.

Van Beek cuts, folds, and layers her source images, adding painted paper and cast shadow to turn flat found pictures into what read as small sculptures, actors staged rather than depicted, borrowing photography's own conventions of shadow, pedestal, and gesture to lend invented objects an unearned authority. New Documents, the Los Angeles art-book publisher, released this 40-page softcover-with-jacket first edition in 2017.

Van Beek studied photography at the Gerrit Rietveld Academy in Amsterdam, where she has taught since 2014, and works from her home in Koog aan de Zaan, near Amsterdam. Her books include The Arrangement (2013) and The Oldest Thing (2023), both shortlisted for the Aperture Photobook of the Year Award; her work has appeared in The New Yorker, Vogue, and Foam Magazine, and she is represented by The Ravestijn Gallery, Amsterdam.
description.artist_bio: Ruth van Beek (b. 1977, the Netherlands) is a Dutch artist and bookmaker who studied photography at the Gerrit Rietveld Academy, Amsterdam, where she has taught since 2014. She works from found photographic material, physically manipulating it into sculptural collage. Represented by The Ravestijn Gallery, Amsterdam; her books The Arrangement (2013) and The Oldest Thing (2023) were both shortlisted for the Aperture Photobook of the Year Award.

notes: Publisher confirmed as New Documents (Los Angeles), not Art Paper Editions or RVB Books as initially guessed in the assignment brief — van Beek's own site (ruthvanbeek.com) lists The Cast under New Documents, matching the publisher's own product page and Printed Matter's listing. No exhibition ties to this title; it reads as a standalone artist book, so classification is set to Individual Artist Monographs. Both New Documents (per book page framing) and Printed Matter list the title as sold out/unavailable, so distributor availability is marked false throughout.
